facts.fact: The Stair plateau has a west lip (a drop) and an old chain of faint cairns; the jogini cairn-light on it shows only at dusk and is dim. Ewe's Rest lies a short descent below the last high cairn.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires crossing the plateau between faint cairns and a dark-fall cairn.

facts.fact: The plateau route-song runs: 'Keep the Crow's Wing on your cheek, keep the cold hollow underfoot, past the stone that split in two, three hundred to where the ewe lay down.' Crow's Wing is a ridge, the cold hollow a scoured dip, and Where the Ewe Lay Down is a waist-high half-ring lambing wall beside the last high cairn.
facts.why: the beat requires a route-song whose names are directions.

facts.fact: The split boulder of the song is buried under a drift. Ila navigates by the bearing of the crag she named (94 degrees at 560 paces) and reaches the wall about forty of Kunal's paces off her predicted line.
facts.why: the beat requires the boulder to be buried and Ila's bearing to prove right.

facts.fact: Ila names a black four-humped crag Nimmi's Knuckle; it has a hill name Kunal refuses to give.
Old Woman's Tooth is a black notched pinnacle north of the lambing wall (bearing 350, about a mile and a quarter) with water under it in spring.
facts.why: the first name in the name trade, per the beat.

facts.fact: Name trade terms: each night Kunal gives one true Neshar name for a feature Ila measured that day, which she writes exactly as he says it; she answers one question about her orders truthfully or refuses for free.
Kunal's palms are rope-scraped and bleeding slightly after the hip belay.
facts.why: consequence of the belay in beat 4.

facts.fact: Ila recites the commission phrase as 'the crown may hold every way' and says she does not know what holding means.
